title: Kernel compatibility checklist for mixed-quant execution paths
summary: Practical compatibility checklist and runbook for mixed-precision inference paths. Focuses on constraints per kernel format (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ), scheduler/hotpath heuristics, and KV-cache coherence checks needed during rollouts.
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a concise, pragmatic checklist and runbook for engineers validating mixed-quant execution paths in the serving runtime. Goal is to reduce surprises when enabling INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ kernels in production by listing per-kernel constraints, scheduling rules, KV cache invariants, required telemetry, and a minimal set of acceptance tests.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: kernel selection and compatibility checks at inference runtime, scheduler hints for low-bit paths, KV cache read/write invariants when weights or execution semantics change, and rollout/runbook steps.
- Non-goals: kernel implementation details, quantization algorithm design, or model training/eval artifacts. Those remain in applied-ml docs.

Assumptions:
- Model artifacts can be tagged with quantization metadata: bitwidth, format (e.g., INT8-symmetric, FP8-e4m3), calibration stats, and decoder compatibility flags.
- Runtime keeps a per-model-version kernel capability manifest (declared by kernel owners).
- KV cache is kept external to kernel ephemeral state and accessed via well-defined APIs.

Quick compatibility checklist (high level):
1) Kernel Manifest Exists: kernel_manifest.json present for model_version with fields: supported_sequence_lengths, max_batch_size, kv_cache_layout, requires_prefix_alignment, deterministic_rng=false/true.
2) Weight Layout Match: runtime verifies runtime.weight_layout == kernel.expected_weight_layout before loading.
3) KV Cache Schema: kernel.compatible_kv_schema must include key ordering and dtype (fp16/int8-perblock).
4) Operator Coverage: all critical attention/matrix ops have fallback (cpu or fp16) if kernel lacks op.
5) Determinism Flag: if kernel sets deterministic_rng=true, ensure downstream tests assert determinism.
6) Fallback Policy: clear policy for per-request fallback (fail-open vs fail-quiet). Default: per-request fallback to FP16 path with trace.

Per-format constraints and runtime checks:
- INT8 (symmetric/affine):
  - Requires per-channel scales in weight metadata. Reject kernel if per-channel scales missing.
  - Expected activation quantization method (min-max, percentile) must match runtime config. Mismatch should surface a warning and require opt-in.
  - Zero-point handling: verify API-level pre/post dequant to maintain residual paths used by KV merge.
  - Memory layout: int8 packed formats often compact blocks; verify weight_block_size modulo 32 alignment.

- FP8 (e4m3/e5m2):
  - Exponent & mantissa policy in kernel manifest. Runtime must track dynamic scaling capability.
  - Check for guaranteed range checks on accumulation path to avoid silent overflow. If kernel lacks saturation checks, runtime must enable bias-correction fallback.
  - KV cache dtypes: if kernel stores keys/values in FP8, ensure conversion path to fp16 exists for downstream ops.

- GPTQ (post-training quantized, per-row codebook):
  - Kernel must expose helper APIs to reconstruct partial rows (for attention patterns that access slices).
  - Sparse/block pattern constraints: runtime must verify that any dynamic slicing respects codebook word boundaries.
  - Serialization compatibility: GPTQ weight shards must include codebook index map; missing map -> reject load.

- AWQ (advanced weight quant, asymmetric + learned scales):
  - Requires explicit scale-encoder in manifest and a small helper JIT for per-layer dequant. Runtime can JIT-compile shim or fallback.
  - Verify that learned-scales are signed and within expected bounds (unit tests assert range).

Scheduler and hotpath heuristics (runtime rules):
- Fast-path selection order for a request: pinned_model_variant -> latency-tier matching -> kernel_cost_estimate (tokens/sec) -> runtime.memory_headroom -> kv-cache-schema-compat.
- Cost estimate includes penalty for FP8->fp16 conversions. Favor pure-dtype paths when target latency < 50ms.
- When batching across mixed-precision variants, prefer partitioning by variant rather than cross-quant fusion. Cross-quant batches are allowed only if all variants share the same kv_cache_layout and activation dtype.
- Prefetching weights: load int8/awq kernel weight shards eagerly when model enters warm state (>200 requests/min). Defer fp8 shards behind an activation threshold due to potential runtime JIT.

KV cache coherence and mutation rules:
- KV cache is the canonical per-session token state. Kernel authors must not persist ephemeral state outside the KV API.
- Layout invariants: runtime asserts kv_layout_signature(session) == model_variant.kv_schema_signature before allowing cache reuse. A mismatch triggers either cache invalidation or transparent per-token conversion depending on policy.
- Conversion modes:
  - Convert-on-load: when loading a model variant with a different kv dtype, perform schema conversion and tag session as upgraded.
  - On-the-fly conversion: inexpensive for fp8<->fp16 when hardware supports vectorized upconvert; otherwise trigger fallback to slow path.
- Concurrency: while converting a live session, block new writes to KV until conversion completes or operate with copy-on-write semantics and reconcile at first read. Documented tradeoffs: blocking increases tail latency, copy-on-write doubles memory.

Telemetry and required traces (release blocking):
- Kernel health metrics: load_time_ms, init_errors, eviction_count, avg_tokens_per_second, avg_memory_bytes.
- Per-request traces must include chosen_kernel_id, variant_cost_estimate, kv_schema_signature, fallback_reason if any.
- Determinism validation traces: sample deterministic_uuid across N runs and assert same token stream when deterministic flag is set.

Acceptance tests (minimal):
- Binary smoke: load model variant with kernel manifest and run a canonical prompt; assert top-1 token distribution close within configured tolerance vs reference fp16 baseline.
- KV roundtrip: warm session, run 10 tokens, snapshot KV, reload variant with identical kv_schema -> assert byte-equal if dtypes same; if conversion expected, assert semantic equivalence within tolerance.
- Fallback stress: induce kernel op error via malformed request and assert runtime falls back to fp16 path within SLO (p95 latency increase within allowed budget).
- Scale test: multi-variant batching test where 1000 concurrent sessions hit mixed quant variants and scheduler keeps p99 latency below target.

Smoke diagnostics and debugging checklist:
- If load fails: collect kernel_manifest, weight_manifest, runtime.env, kernel_init.log.
- If numeric anomalies: run per-layer activations diff against fp16 baseline with 5 random seeds and log max-abs relative error per layer.
- If KV mismatch: export kv_layout_signature and a minimal repro that triggers conversion path.

Runbook for enabling a new quant kernel in prod (short):
1) Canary stage (dev infra): add kernel manifest to model build and run unit smoke tests.
2) Internal alpha (limited org): enable on 1% of traffic with forced-fallback off. Monitor kernel_health and token-accuracy.
3) Beta (broad org): enable on 10% traffic with fallback enabled and conversion logging detailed. Collect error budget delta.
4) Gradual rollout: 10->25->50->100% with 24h hold at each step and a rollback gate if any of these triggers fire: 
   - error_rate increase > 3x baseline,
   - p99 latency regression > 20%,
   - accuracy drift measured on steady prompts outside tolerance.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Should we standardize a minimal kernel manifest schema across all kernel teams (proposal: v1 manifest limited to 12 fields)?
- What is the long-term strategy for on-the-fly FP8->FP16 conversions in terms of memory pressure?
- Do we expose a developer API to request a specific kernel by id for debugging? If so, what auth model?

Appendix: short repro snippets and commands (engineer-friendly)
- Inspect manifest: runtime-cli model inspect --model <id> --variant <v> --show-kernel-manifest
- Force-fallback test: runtime-cli request --model <id> --variant <v> --force-fallback=fp16 --prompt-file tests/short_prompts.json
- Export KV: runtime-cli session export-kv --session <sid> --out /tmp/kv.dump

Notes: this checklist is intentionally conservative — prefer safe rollouts with precise telemetry over aggressive early enabling. If you add a new kernel, please append a short summary of deviations and known gotchas to this doc and ping #eng-serving-runtime for coordination.
acceptance_criteria: All items in the Acceptance tests section pass on the canary infra and telemetry for kernel_health is present. Team lead signoff required before internal alpha.
test_plan: Automated unit smoke scripts in infra/test-kernel-smoke; nightly regression runs comparing fp16 baseline to quant variants; dedicated stress job in prod-sim cluster that simulates p99 loads.
rollout_notes: Start with dev canary -> internal alpha (1%) -> beta (10%) -> gradual. Enable verbose conversion logging for first 72 hours after each step. Have immediate rollback flag in control plane.
open_questions: 1) kernel manifest v1 schema approval. 2) conversion memory budget thresholds. 3) debug API access control.
final_notes: If you make a runtime change that affects fallback semantics, update the rollout gates and add a short rationale in this doc. Keep this file as the single runbook reference for mixed-quant kernel rollouts.
